how_to_apply: Email a cover letter, resume, three references, and a brief writing sample all in one PDF file, with the file name including internship class, year, last name, and first name (e.g. Spring2025.Doe.Jane.pdf) to CA49.DCInternships@mail.house.gov by November 15, 2024. Specify whether you are applying for the press internship or the legislative internship.
equal_opportunity: This office is an equal opportunity employer; we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, gender identity or expression, or sexual orientation. We deeply value the diversity of our employees and encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply.

description: Internships in the Office of Congressman Tim Kennedy are available for the fall, spring, and summer sessions for college students and recent graduates. Students will gain invaluable experience working for a member of Congress alongside congressional staff. Hours can be flexible to accommodate academic schedules. In Washington, D.C. and the Buffalo District Office, intern responsibilities vary, but typically include answering phones, administrative duties, legislative research, attending hearings, meetings, and briefings, drafting correspondence, letters, and Congressional Extensions of Remarks, and assisting with media monitoring. In addition, interns may be assigned to assist in various constituent casework or assist with district-based projects. As a result, interns learn about the legislative process and the many other functions of a congressional office.
responsibilities: Drafting correspondence, letters, and Congressional Extensions of Remarks
qualifications: College student or recent graduate
Interest in the legislative process and congressional office functions

equal_opportunity: We do not discriminate based on race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, religion, national origin, age, or socioeconomic status. All are welcome and encouraged to apply.

The deadline for this internship application is November 1st, 2024, but applicants are encouraged to submit their application early. Interview requests will be sent out following the November 1st deadline. For more information visit: https://morelle.house.gov/congressional-internships

description: The Office of Congresswoman Kim Schrier (WA-08) is seeking interns in its Issaquah and Washington, D.C. offices for spring 2025. Applicants should be eager to learn more about the legislative process and want to be part of a hardworking team dedicated to serving Washington's 8th Congressional District. Interns will work in a fast-paced Congressional office, gaining valuable experience and knowledge of the United States Congress. In Washington, D.C., intern responsibilities will include greeting constituents, answering constituent phone calls, supporting staff with administrative tasks, conducting legislative research, assisting with constituent correspondence, and other miscellaneous tasks as assigned. Interns in Washington, D.C. also have the opportunity to lead tours of the U.S. Capitol, as well as attend briefings for the legislative staff. In the District office, interns will assist with a variety of tasks, including day-to-day office work such as answering phones, writing letters, and assisting with media clips. District office interns may also help with constituent casework or other District-based projects of importance. Starting and ending dates are flexible, although prospective interns should be able to commit at least 20 hours per week during business hours. Congressional internships are open to all majors and designed for undergraduate and graduate students, as well as recent graduates with an interest in public service. Stipends or academic credit are available. Please apply by November 15, 2024, at 11:59 p.m. ET.
